newsitem.title: FRANCE: TNT plans "direct" Paris-US shipments in 97.
newsitem.headline: TNT plans "direct" Paris-US shipments in 97.

text.p: TNT Express Worldwide said it plans to offer "direct" routes for express shipments from Paris to the U.S., effective January 1997 via block space agreements on scheduled passenger and freighter services.

"Since end-October, we have been using Air France and Singapore Airlines Boeing 747 flights to Tokyo and Singapore, on a daily basis, for documents and parcels with a maximum unit weight of 30 kilos," TNT France air transport operations manager, Pierre Izard told Reuters.
"We now intend to extend this type of service on scheduled flights from Paris to New York and to Miami," he added.
Previously, TNT's ex-Paris shipments bound for the Far East were transported via London which had entailed intermediate handling and longer delivery deadlines, Izard said.
"With direct services from Paris to Tokyo and Singapore, we are reducing transit times by one day and are able to offer customers delivery deadlines of around 48 hours."
TNT is carrying 700 to 800 kg of shipments each day on SIA's service to Singapore and approximately 500 kg daily on Air France's Paris-Tokyo route, Izzard added.
"We are happy with the start we've made and are banking on a steady build-up in volumes."

As for new services on transatlantic routes, TNT currently transports ex-Paris shipments destined for New York via dedicated flights from its European hub at Cologne. Shipments destined for Miami are also handled at New York.
"Direct routes from Paris to New York and Miami will clearly lead to reductions in transit times while Miami would serve as an important hub for traffic to South America."
TNT had been in discussions with Air France on possible block space agreements on the airline's flights to New York and Miami and it expects to finalise the plans later this month, Izard said.
The express operator is also looking to develop a similar service to other Far East destinations, including Shanghai and Hong Kong.

"We had planned to launch an ex-Paris service to Shanghai during December using SIA's Paris-Singapore-Shanghai route but this depends on clearance from the Chinese customs authorities," he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
